_comment: D-128 tiered gates. code = hard block; docs/recon = advisory. Unknown => code (fail safe). enforce_since_ts (unix) grandfathers tasks completed/created before it (D-132 addendum); 0 = enforce for all. D-165: a tier name that does not exist in `tiers` is ignored (next source wins, default_tier last) so a typo can never fail open.

ci_evidence._comment: D-132: invoke ngit_ci_evidence.py for the exact head; no_results/timeout/nak-missing all block. t_7c503759 (2026-09-22): limit knob threads a nak `-l` to the tool so a busy relay's newest-first window cannot hide a repo's results; server-side `#c` commit filter is primary, this is the fallback depth.

recon._comment: D-165: read-only recon / inventory / measurement cards (no repo, no commit, no PR, no CI workflow). Advisory — it can never block a card. Keeps the two checks that ARE meaningful for read-only work: a written review artifact and an independently re-scanned clean secret scan. tests_green/ci_evidence/push are deliberately NOT required because they are structurally impossible for this class of work.

delivery._comment: D-144 (2026-10-05): delivery-only cards publish an artifact instead of shipping code, so code gates (tests_green, ci_evidence, consolidated) are unsatisfiable. A done card was re-dispatched every 10 minutes for exactly this reason, burning a worker session per pass on a merged deliverable.

task_waivers._comment: Operator-approved per-task carve-outs. Key = 'board:task' (or bare task). A listed task returns verdict=waived and skips ALL code-tier gates — used only where the deliverable is genuinely done/merged/CI-green but some mandatory gates are structurally unsatisfiable (ci_evidence tooling reads ngit while the repo is GitHub-Actions-routed; pr_branch_naming vs a D-116-mandated non-pr/ branch). Additions require an explicit operator decision; the MANDATORY_CODE_GATES floor holds for every other card.
